title: When People Laughed at Index Funds
content: [laughter] You know index funds were a punchline once? Early on, the people selling them couldn't raise anything close to what they hoped for. The rest of the industry laughed. They called it 'settling for average.' Somebody actually called it un-American - why would anyone choose to just be average? Well... [laughter] ...turns out most people would LOVE average returns, because most actively managed funds don't even get there after fees. That punchline now holds a staggering share of the money people are retiring on.
follow_up: The lesson for me is: sometimes what looks like failure in the moment is just the beginning of something revolutionary.
